datasets.title: Chad Displacement Data - Site & Village Assessment - Lac Province - [IOM DTM]
datasets.description: A site assessment is a sub-component of mobility tracking. It aims to collect data on population presence, living conditions and needs in a particular displacement site or community.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/chad-site-village-assessment-lac-province-data-iom-dtm]

entity.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)

lineage.description: IOM DTM conducted repeated site and village assessments in Lac Province, Chad using standardized methodology to enumerate internally displaced persons, returnees, and affected populations. Data were collected across 25 rounds documenting displacement status, household counts, demographic breakdowns by age and gender, and origin provinces. The dataset captures post-displacement impact records with particular attention to flood-triggered displacement events.

sources.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
sources.description: Site and village assessments documenting population presence, displacement status, and demographic composition in Lac Province. Data collected through standardized DTM methodology across 25 assessment rounds.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 25
resources.description: The MSLA round 25 data were collected from 17 September to 18 October 2025 across 287 locations, representing a decrease of nine locations compared to Round 24. In terms of the total displaced population, a 3% decrease was recorded compared to round 24. MSLA round 25 recorded 259,839 individuals (equivalent to 58,931 households), comprising: 219,595 IDPs (85%) 24,165 returnees former IDPs (9%) 16,079 returnees from abroad (6%) The Fouli department hosts the highest concentration of displaced individuals (47% of the total displaced population). The dataset includes a detailed breakdown of displaced populations by department and sub‑prefecture.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 24
resources.description: This dataset presents the results of evaluations conducted between December 9, 2024, and January 14, 2025, in 296 displacement sites and villages. During this round, DTM identified 225,689 IDPs, 11,117 returnees from abroad, and 25,248 internal returnees. Comparing Round 24 with Round 23 in terms of the total displaced population, we observe a slight increase of 2 percent in Round 24, representing more than 5,000 people.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 23
resources.description: This dataset presents the results of evaluations conducted between May 7 and June 8, 2024, in 293 displacement locations. Comparing Round 23 with Round 22 in terms of the total displaced population, we observe a slight increase of 0.2%, which is insignificant as it represents fewer than 500 people.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 22
resources.description: From December 22nd 2023 to January 24th 2024, the DTM Chad has conducted the round 22 of Sites and Villages assessment accross 305 locations. During this round, a total of 261,672 displaced individuals were identified, including 219.393 internally displaced persons, 25,007internal returnees and 17,272 returnees from abroad.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 21
resources.description: From October 5th 2023 to November 8th 2023, the DTM team in Chad has conducted the round 21 of Sites and Villages assessment accross 281 locations. During this round, a total of 242,205 displaced individuals were identified, including 199,198 internally displaced persons, 27,090 internal returnees and 15,718 returnees from abroad.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 20
resources.description: This dataset contains the results of evaluations conducted between 26 March - 08 May 2023 in 249 places of displacement. There was an overall increase of 2% over the previous round. This slight increase can be attributed to the fact that the evaluation was carried out during the period of Ramadan, during which some communities return to be with family. This is also due to the 4% increase in IDPs due to the increase in new displacement in April due to armed attacks and fear (ETT 166). It should be noted that in the Round 20 key informants reported 14% of sites hosting people displaced by flooding.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 19
resources.description: This dataset contains the results of evaluations conducted between November 29, 2022 - January 9, 2023 in 245 locations. A slight increase in the number of displaced people was observed during this round 19 compared to the previous round (+6%). This is mainly explained by the displacements due to floods and insecurity during this period. During this round, a total number of 255,054 individuals were displaced, including 207,691 internal displaced individuals, 28,660 returnees from abroad and 18,703 internal returnees.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 18
resources.description: This dataset presents the results of evaluations conducted between June 8 and July 18, 2022 in 240 locations of displacement (villages and sites). During this assessment, a total number of 239,576 displaced persons have been reported, including 200,031 individuals internally displaced, and 22,599 individuals returned from abroad and 16,946 individuals internally returned.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 17
resources.description: This dataset presents the results of evaluations conducted between November 12 and December 27, 2021 in 253 places of displacement (villages and sites). A seven percent decrease in the number of displaced persons was observed during this round 17 compared to the previous round.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 11
resources.description: April 2020 During the data collection, a 13 percent increase in the number of IDPs was observed compared to the previous round, mainly as a result of the displacement of people from the insular border areas of Niger and Nigeria to the mainland, following military operations launched by the government against armed groups operating in the region.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 10
resources.description: Jan-Feb 2020 272478 Individuals and 59761 households. Evaluations carried out between January 15 and February 26, 2020 in 204 places of displacement. In assessments, a 23 percent increase in the number of displaced persons was observed.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 8
resources.description: As of April 2019, 178,928 displaced individuals (43,359 Households), including 133,338 IDPs, 42,788 Returnees and 2,802 Third Country Nationals (TCNs) were identified in 189 locations (134 sites and 55 host communities). 67% of displaced individuals were children, while 3% were 60 years old or older. An overlwheming majority (95%) of displaced individuals live in a shelter made of straw or metal sheet.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 7
resources.description: As of February 2019, 174,340 displaced individuals (43,291 Households), including 130,472 IDPs, 41,199 Returnees and 2,669 Third Country Nationals (TCNs) were identified in 185 locations (131 sites and 53 host communities). 67% of displaced individuals were children, while 2% were 60 years old or older. An overlwheming majority (95%) of displaced individuals live in a shelter made of straw or metal sheet.

resources.title: DTM Chad Site and Village Assessment Round 6
resources.description: As of December 2018, 167,246 displaced individuals (41,620 Households), including 126,313 IDPs, 39,312 Returnees and 1,621 Third Country Nationals (TCNs) were identified in 176 locations (123 sites and 53 host communities). 67% of displaced individuals were children, while 3% were 60 years old or older, and all displaced households (100%) had children. Most (92%) identified displaced individuals live in a shelter made of straw or metal sheet.
